name: The Third Plane of Rathauspark
verified_sources: data/registers/wien-naturdenkmale.json (Naturdenkmal register_id 3257650, city of Vienna MA22 designation, species Platanus x hybrida, place '1., Rathauspark')

https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Wien/Innere_Stadt (confirms three individually protected planes in Rathauspark, Naturdenkmal Nr. 564, 566 and 567, all protected 3 July 1973; ND 564 is vie_006, one of 566/567 is vie_026, this is the remaining one)
data.wien.gv.at WFS layer ogdwien:BAUMKATOGD (Vienna city tree cadastre, BAUM_ID 147511: PFLANZJAHR 1873, STAMMUMFANG 526 cm, 2.9 m from the register point)
access: Free, public park, open at all times
transport: 3 min walk from Rathaus U-Bahn station (U2) or the Rathausplatz tram stop (Tram 1/71/D)
verify_notes: This completes the set: Rathauspark has exactly three individually protected planes (Naturdenkmal Nr. 564, 566, 567, all designated 3 July 1973). vie_006 is Nr. 564 (the 'Founding Plane', catalogue no. 252, register_id 3257649) and vie_026 is one of the other two (register_id 3257651, girth 597 cm). This tree is register_id 3257650, the remaining one, standing 55 m from vie_026 (baum_id 147511 vs 147537, girth 526 cm vs 597 cm, genuinely distinct trees, not the same specimen mismeasured). An earlier verify pass held this one back on a padding concern ('three planes in one park'); it is not padding, it is the third and final member of a designation that already exists as a set of three, same as the other two already published. Age: the city's own tree register gives 1873 to every protected tree in this park (the year the park was laid out around the new Rathaus), which is what a register writes when a whole park is planted at once, so treat 1873 as documented-but-blanket rather than a ring count, same caveat as vie_006 and vie_026. Girth 526 cm is the smallest of the park's three protected planes (526 vs 534 vs 597 vs the beech's 600, per the Baumkataster query already run for vie_013), still a substantial trunk. No dispute, no access issue: same public park as three already-published trees.

name: The Black Pine of Ebner-Eschenbach-Park
age_estimate: not documented; protected as a natural monument since 1942
verified_sources: data/registers/wien-naturdenkmale.json (Naturdenkmal register_id 3257378, city of Vienna MA22 designation, species Pinus nigra, place '18., Klostergasse')

https://www.wien.gv.at/umweltschutz/naturschutz/gebiet/naturdenkmaeler/bezirk-18.html (city's own district-18 Naturdenkmal list, confirms 'Klostergasse, Ebner-Eschenbach-Park' as the location for this designation)

https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Wien/W%C3%A4hring (Naturdenkmal Nr. 333, protected 16.11.1942, protection reasoning cites the tree's size, appearance and role in the park landscape)
access: Free, public city park (Ebner-Eschenbach-Park, 6,200 sqm, run by the city of Vienna, playgrounds and open lawns), open at all times
transport: Tram 9 or 41/42 to Gersthofer Strasse / Sternwartestrasse area, then a short walk; roughly 10 min walk from Waehring-Geblergasse or Gersthof stations
verify_notes: Verified as standing inside Ebner-Eschenbach-Park itself, not a private courtyard: this address (Klostergasse) is one of the streets that borders the park (confirmed via search: the park is 'surrounded by Staudgasse, Lacknergasse, Paulinengasse, and Klostergasse'), and both the register and the city's own official Naturdenkmal district-18 page independently give the location as 'Klostergasse, Ebner-Eschenbach-Park', not a street number. This distinguishes it from several other nearby register entries in the same Wahring 'Cottage' area (Paulinengasse 9 'Innenhof des Lindenhofes', Koehlergasse 20 'im Garten hinter dem Gebaeude', Lacknergasse 79 'behind building') which ARE private-courtyard trees and were left as leads below, and from Klostergasse 37 (a plain street-number address, likely private, also left as a lead). No girth, height or age figure found in any of the three sources checked this pass (register, wien.gv.at, German Wikipedia); only the 1942 protection date is documented, which implies the tree was already notable by then but does not by itself support a numeric age estimate, so age_estimate is left descriptive rather than a derived figure. Nearest published Vienna tree is vie_010 (Twin Giants of Sternwartepark), about 0.85 km away, so this extends rather than joins that Wahring-area walk. Species Pinus nigra confirmed consistently across all three sources; no conflicting identification found.

name: The Sessile Oak of Belvedereallee
verified_sources: data/registers/wien-naturdenkmale.json (Naturdenkmal register_id 3257960, city of Vienna MA22 designation, species Quercus petraea, place '2., Prater - Belvedereallee', monument_type Einzelbaum i.e. an individual tree, not a group designation)

https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Wien/Leopoldstadt (Naturdenkmal Nr. 818, girth 4.50 m at 1 m height, crown diameter roughly 29 m, height roughly 30 m, protected 8 Feb 2009, location 'Prater - Belvedereallee' confirmed as public park land)
access: Free, in the Prater (Vienna's largest public park), open at all times
transport: Bus 77A to 'Freudenau' or 'Lusthaus', then a short walk; a longer alternative is the Hauptallee on foot from Praterstern (U1/U2), roughly 45 minutes
verify_notes: A large sessile oak on public land in the Prater, well away from the Hauptallee chestnut avenue already published as vie_003 (about 1.8 km away), so this is a separate stop rather than an extension of that walk; label it honestly as a distinct part of the Prater rather than implying it is on the same path. Girth 4.50 m at 1 m height and a crown around 29 m wide are both from the German Wikipedia Leopoldstadt Naturdenkmal list (Nr. 818), which also gives the protection date (8 Feb 2009) and explicitly reads as public park land, unlike several other Prater-area candidates checked this pass and rejected: the four Meiereistrasse 3 planes (register_ids 3257979-3257982, same Leopoldstadt Wikipedia list, explicitly noted as standing on a sculptor's studio site, 'Bildhaueratelier' grounds, i.e. private, and recorded as blocked below) and the Prater yew group (Nr. 806, a 9-tree group designation, excluded under the standing group-designation rule regardless of access). No age figure found in any source; girth alone was not used to derive one this pass given uncertainty about growth conditions in parkland versus open floodplain forest (this part of the Prater is remnant floodplain forest per Wikipedia's Wiener Prater article), so age_estimate is left as not documented rather than guessed. Species Quercus petraea agrees between the register and the Wikipedia list; no conflicting identification found. Exact coordinates are the register's own tree-level point.
